applies_why: The judge text does not rest its UNDERDETERMINED ruling on a single verse's failure to state a link or its contrary; it rests on a balance of the two chains.
quote: D5 vs C1 (Acts 2:30): UNDERDETERMINED -- [CR2] and [CR3] answered the loins/seed row with Genesis 46:26 and Hebrews 7:10 (loins at depth) and the legal/flesh distinction, while [DR3] presses that the only named Davidic man is Joseph; neither chain forces the other.
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: The phrase 'That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED' — I weighed (1) it bars only an express single-verse-silence ground, not a balance-of-chains ground; (2) it bars any underdetermination that relies on a verse not settling the issue.
why: The judge's stated reason is that neither chain forces the other, not that Acts 2:30 alone fails to state the link or its contrary.
